data.note: You need to know PED compares percentage changes before you can calculate it.

plan.cue: Ask the check on this point with these lettered options; wait for a letter.

options.text: Work out the percentage changes from the new values.
Divide the change in price by the change in quantity.
PED is the change in quantity divided by the change in price, with no percentages.

notes.summary: PED equals the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. Work out each percentage change from the original value first, then divide.
key_wording: % change in quantity demanded divided by % change in price
notes.source: Example Economics Textbook (invented for this pack)

style.format: Write formulas in LaTeX between $$…$$, e.g. $$PED = \frac{\%\Delta Q_d}{\%\Delta P}$$. Write money as £5, or escape a dollar sign as \$, because $ starts maths. For a diagram part, or when the student asks for one, draw the diagram inline as an SVG visual with labelled axes, the curves, the shift and P1→P2 / Q1→Q2 marked; never use ASCII art. Don't draw otherwise: drawing is slow.
